chunks: So al-Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Miskān, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

I asked him about a man who was on a journey and had water with him, but forgot it, so he performed tayammum and prayed, then remembered that he had water with him before the time had ended. He said: “He must perform wudu (ablution) and repeat the salat (prayer).” He said: And I asked him whether the tayammum of the menstruating woman and the junub is the same when they do not find water. He said: “Yes.”

key_terms.سَفَرٍ: travel or journey, the state in which the scenario takes place
key_terms.فَتَيَمَّمَ: he performed tayammum, dry ablution in place of water
key_terms.نَعَمْ: an affirmative answer indicating the ruling is the same
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةَ: the ritual prayer that must be repeated in this case
key_terms.ٱلْجُنُبِ: the person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets that water is available and performs tayammum, must the salat (prayer) be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on tayammum when water was actually available but forgotten during travel. It also states that the tayammum of a menstruating woman and a junub is the same when neither finds water.
